Man, i need to brush up on my knowledge of tune types… I THINK this is a slip jig… (?)
Donal Lunny wrote this, it’s a fun tune but you’ll go insane after practicing it a few times… oh well :)

↳ Posted by Mark de Jong on July 21st, 2002.

Oh yeah, on the last line, after you play the second ending you’re supposed to go back to the beginning, play the whole thing through, and on then skip the last second ending and go to the part after it. Confusing??

↳ Posted by Mark de Jong on July 22nd, 2002.

Great tune

This is a great slip jig. Fair play to you for writing all of it out in ABC.

That Donal Lunny live album with this tune on it is one of the best trad recordings ever, in my humble opinion. It has that terrific version of The Gold Ring and those mad polkas.

Does anyone have the track listing for it? And, if so, would they like to post it in the “Recordings” section?

↳ Posted by Jeremy on July 22nd, 2002.

Thats brilliant Mark, well done

Thanks for writing this out in the abc thing.
It took me ages to learn it of the CD and then write it down.

For anyone else who wants to learn it, don’t give up, it’s worth it.
Just play along with the CD, and the dots should help.

↳ Posted by Michael C. Gill on July 24th, 2002.

Brilliant, but there are a few bars that differ from what is played on the recording:

A-part bars 5&6: |ABc cde dcA|BAG dBG cGE|
B-part bar 5: |cde dgf ~e2d|
C-part bar 1: |efg eaf dgf|
C-part bar 6: |def gdB cGE|
E-part bar 2: |cde dBG cGE|

↳ Posted by Dr. Dow on March 4th, 2006.

Leppadumdowledum

I’ve been asked to submit a full transcription here with the corrections for this tune. This is based on the pipes setting. ~D3 denotes a low D cran. If you want to convert this to sheetmusic, cut & paste the abc with all its headers including the X: header into the box @ this webpage http://www.concertina.net/tunes_convert.html and click on “submit”. If you like pretty dots, download it as a pdf.

X: 1
T: Leppadumdowledum
C: Donal Lunny
M: 9/8
L: 1/8
R: slip jig
K: Dmix
ABc cBA GAB|BAG cGE GED|~D3 GFD ~D3|~D3 GFD DE/2F/2G|

e2d gfe faf|def gdB cGE|~D3 GFD ~D3|1 ~D3 GFD Dcd:|2 ~D3 GFD d2c||
|:Bdg dBd edc|Bdg dBc dBG|c2B A2G AdB|c2B A2G Adc|
